review_notes: I read the whole file and searched the repository for uses of `amnrStateDerivative_uncurry_eq` and for the definitions of `amnrStateDerivative` and `jointSpatialFDeriv`. The file has only one rewrite-style lemma, so the only simp-interface point is its missing normalisation attribute. I did not check whether other simp lemmas about `jointSpatialFDeriv` would interact with it, and I did not run Lean, so the proposal is untested.

findings.excerpt:
theorem amnrStateDerivative_uncurry_eq (b : ℝ → Vec 2 → Vec 2) (t : ℝ) (x : Vec 2) :
    amnrStateDerivative (Function.uncurry b) (t, x) = jointSpatialFDeriv b t x := rfl
findings.problem: This is a definitional rewrite from the generic `amnrStateDerivative (Function.uncurry b) (t, x)` to the canonical `jointSpatialFDeriv b t x`. It has no simp attribute, so every caller must name it explicitly. The file does this in `simpa only [norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero, amnrStateDerivative_uncurry_eq]` (line 61) and `simpa only [amnrStateDerivative_uncurry_eq]` (line 71). FlowGlobalJointSmoothness.lean line 48 does the same. Without the attribute, a `simp` call or `simpa using` call that meets the generic form will not normalise it.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`. The left side is the more complex generic form and the right side is the specialised canonical form, so the orientation is right and the rule cannot cycle. The call sites can then use `simpa [norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero] using ...`, or plain `simpa using ...`, without naming the lemma. The check-in comment should say that `jointSpatialFDeriv` is the normal form.
findings.benefit: Statements that arise from `amnrCurveJacobianCoefficient_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le` (which is stated with `amnrStateDerivative`) are converted to `jointSpatialFDeriv` automatically. The three call sites in two files no longer repeat the lemma name in `simpa only`.
